Keep the send route type private to the module that decides it

Name the melt quote when a payment says it is processing

A melt confirmed from a preview executes against the quote the preview
created, and every later wallet event of that melt carries the quote id.
The processing notification now carries it too, so the app can tie the
payment's toast to its own melt from the start.
Format the wallet manager lifecycle test and drop a storage mock it never needed

Pin a payment toast confirmed or failed by its own melt or send

A processing melt toast confirmed in place by its melt with that melt's
operation for View, a delivered payment-request toast confirmed by its
send, and no second failed toast for a rollback the payment flow already
reported.

Save an AI question and its answer's place in one write

The question and the empty answer it waits for were added in two writes, so
a kill between them saved a question with no answer and nothing to press.
They are now added together. Also pinned: a question saved as still sending,
by a kill or an older build, loads as sent with its answer read as one to ask
again, and regenerating it works.

Decide where an ecash send goes in one place

The amount screen and the send's completion each read the nearby and contact
stores in their own order of checks to decide whether the token goes over the
mesh, to a contact or onto the hand-off screen. Both now take one route value
from sendRouteOf and switch on it. No entry point sets both; were both set, the
nearby recipient now wins at completion too, as the amount screen already
showed, instead of the token being messaged to the contact.

Keep an AI answer that stopped partway, as one to ask again

Leaving the screen mid-answer, or a newer stream stopping an older one,
deleted the answer: the question was left with no answer and nothing to
press. The answer now stays, showing the text that had arrived and saying it
stopped before it finished, with Retry. That text is kept in memory only: the
saved answer stays empty, so after a restart it reads as an answer that never
arrived, as before.

Delete the AI top-up through Send, which nothing starts any more

Send's completion paid the token to Routstr when a top-up store said a
top-up was active, but nothing in the app sets it: its start was called only
from tests. The branch, the store, its reads on the amount screens and in
clearPaymentContext, its balance formatter and three toasts only that branch
showed are gone. Topping up from the AI screen is unchanged, and
executeRoutstrTopUp stays with its test.

Delete a recovery's stale mint operations only where it restored the mint

The end of a recovery run listed and deleted every pending mint operation
on the ground that the proofs had been recovered. That was false for a
mint whose restore failed, timed out, or was skipped (all its keysets
unrestorable, or the run stopped first), and for operations that appeared
while the run went on: the records a later retry would need were deleted
(F210). Pending operations are now read before anything is restored, and
at the end only those still pending, on a mint this run restored, are
deleted. A mint the Stop cut short before its last keyset now ends skipped
(Cancelled) instead of done, since it was not recovered. Nothing is deleted
that was not deleted before.
Give the turn tests an error id the catalogue has

Hold a recovery run as one value with one owner

The run's phase was spread over the screen's phase, results, error
message and label, a mutable results array, and two module flags for
the single run and for Stop. It is now one value (idle, running, cancelling
or finished with how it ended), moved by one transition, and owned by the
run in recoveryRun.ts, which decides Stop and each mint's timeout and the
end from the mints' rows. Each row is a union by status carrying only what
that status needs, with a timed-out mint now a status of its own rather
than a failed row with a 'Timed out' message; it reads and counts as before.
The screen renders the value and shows the popups for how it ended.

Say where each AI answer stands in one turn, owned by its message

An answer's state was split across the send hook's status, a live-text
buffer with one slot, an error map and a truncation map each capped at 24,
and the bubble rebuilt the phase from all four. One turn per answer, keyed by
its message id, now says it: asking, streaming with the text so far, done
(with the budget note when it ran out), failed and why, or interrupted. The
send hook moves it through a pure transition, a settled turn ignores late
events, and the bubble and screen only read it. A saved answer with no turn
reads as before: done if it holds text, interrupted if empty. An error no
longer falls back to the generic interrupted copy after 24 others.

Type the melt state read and the reconciler test's read ids

Follow-up to the two previous swap commits: the engine's melt state can
be undefined, and the test maps calls of a mock typed with no arguments.

Keep the wallet manager's open, ready and closing in one state

The manager's life was five statics read together: the instance, the
database, the open in flight, the close in flight and whether the close
failed. It is now one value, closed, opening, ready or closing, and each
state holds what it owns: an open the database it has opened, a ready
wallet its manager and database, a close the wallet it is tearing down.
Every initialize joins the one open, readiness is the ready state, and a
close reports whether it was complete instead of setting a flag. Callers
keep the same methods. Tests that set the private instance now set the
state; the lifecycle pin's database stand-in gets the type its close needs.

Keep a timed-out mint timed out when its late restore result arrives

The recovery timeout cancels nothing, so a mint that timed out goes on
restoring; when it finished after the run had ended it rewrote its row
from timed out to done, and the screen's counts with it (part of F178).
A mint's outcome is now final: once a row has one, nothing changes it.
The restore itself still runs on in the background, as before.

Keep a newer AI answer's live text when the stream it stopped ends

When a send overlapped a regenerated answer, the newer stream stopped the
older one, and the older one's cleanup then cleared the live text and the
sending state the newer one owned, so the answer still streaming showed
nothing until it finished. Each stream's cleanup now touches only its own.

Save an AI answer in the conversation that asked, whichever is open

Opening another conversation or starting a new one while an answer streamed
lost the paid answer: its writes went to whichever conversation was open when
it finished, so the old one kept an empty answer and its question stayed
marked as sending. The send now records the conversation it was asked in, and
the answer, the question's sent mark, the title and the payment's label are
written there.

Pin how a recovery run stops, ends and cleans up, and a remount mid-run

Stopping between keysets or during the search of discovered mints, the
deletion of every pending mint operation at the end (QUIRK: also for a
mint whose restore failed or was cut short, F210), cleanup that cannot
list or delete, and a screen mounted again while a run goes on.

Close the wallet database when an open fails after opening it

When the wallet's tables could not be set up after its database had opened,
the open failed but left that handle open, outside anything that closes it:
a close found no wallet and returned, and the next open opened a second
handle on the same file. A failed open now closes the database it opened.
Nothing is deleted.

Hand out the wallet only once its plugins have started

The manager published the wallet before its plugins had started, so a
second open in that window got a wallet that was not ready, and when the
plugins failed every later open was handed that failed wallet. The wallet
is now published after its plugins start; one whose plugins fail is closed
with its database, and the next open starts afresh. An open overtaken by
delete-all while its plugins started is discarded as before.

Pin how the wallet manager opens and closes for its callers

Concurrent opens share one database open, an open wallet is handed back as
it is, a failed database open is tried again, a close closes the database
once and the next open is a new wallet, an open that asks during a close
waits for it, an incomplete close is reported to a caller that needs it, and
a close during an open closes what that open built.
Type the indexer wait's timer for both platforms' setTimeout

Pin a follow one relay refused, and a tap made across an account switch

A follow that only some write relays took is settled, and the next follow is
built on it and brings the other relays up to it. The Follow button writes
into whichever account's stores are loaded; no screen can tap it while they
change, since both switch flows unmount the screens first.

Stop waiting for the indexers once their bookkeeping ceiling has passed

A first follow waited for the facade's final update with no limit, so an
update that never came held the account's follow worker until a restart. It
now waits for the data layer's per-source ceiling plus five seconds, then
treats the indexers as unanswered: the follow waits and nothing is published.

Wake a waiting follow on a same-second list and on a write relay connecting

A follow waiting on a list from the same second, or on a write relay that
did not answer, stayed put until the next tap or return to the foreground:
the hook woke only when the list's time changed. It now also wakes when the
store takes in a list from the same second and when a write relay connects.

Count only a non-empty string as a payment request entry's operation id

The phase decoder took any truthy value that was not the preview id as proof
the request had run, where the merge it replaced required a string. An entry
whose operation id was a number or a flag would have hidden Pay on a request
that never sent. Writers only ever write strings; anything else now names no
operation.

Carry a payment on when the host's start or failure notification throws

A notification that threw as a melt or payment request started, or as one
failed or was cancelled, left the machine held and executing, and rejected Pay
without its outcome: an undelivered request already recorded never reached
its caller. One that rejected later became an unhandled rejection. These
notifications are now called fire and forget: a throw or rejection is logged,
the payment and the turn carry on, and Pay resolves its outcome.

Keep the lower id of two follow lists from the same second

The social store took any list with the same created_at as the one it held,
and the follow worker saved its read before checking it, so a same-second
list that relays keep (the lower id) was replaced by the one the write relays
returned and a follow was built on that. The store now keeps the id of the
list it took in this session (in memory only: the saved fields hold none) and
lets the lower id win. The worker plans on the store as it was before the
read, waits when the store knows a list relays keep over the read, and waits
when the store holds a different list from the same second whose id it does
not know, and keeps the read only once the plan stands on it.

Let an NFC tap a reset overtook release the tag and switch the unit back

A tap overtaken by a reset while it switched the unit, checked a mint, created
or wrote the token, or released the tag stopped where it stood: the tag
session stayed open and the wallet stayed on the terminal's unit. Such a tap
still changes no step and runs no handler, but now ends like any other: it
releases the session and switches the unit back, unless its token reached the
tag.

Record an NFC payment once the token is on the tag, whatever the release does

When the tag took the token but the session then failed to close, the
write-back treated it as a failed payment: it tried to take the ecash back,
and when the receiver had already redeemed it, reported an error with nothing
recorded. The machine sat on an error holding the request, ready to send it
again. Once the token is written the payment is delivered; a release that
fails afterwards is logged and undoes nothing.

Wait for the account's relay list before reading or publishing a follow

A relay list that had not loaded read as the default relays, so a follow
could be built on, and sent to, relays the account's list is not on. The
worker now waits until the list is known (loaded, or found missing by this
session's relay-list sync, which is remembered in memory only), wakes when it
loads or changes, and reads again if the write relays changed before the
publish.

Read a swap leg again when it changed while its operation was read

The reconciler refuses to apply a result to a leg that changed while its
operation was being read, but then waited for the next operation event or
a reopen before looking at the leg again. A pass whose write was refused
that way is now followed by one more pass, once.

Keep nothing of a request an NFC tap paid, so choosing a mint cannot pay it again

After a tap paid a request and showed it sent, the flow still held the
request, its amount and its mint. Choosing a mint or an amount from there
resolved the old request into a fresh preview, and Pay sent it a second time.
A paid tap now leaves the flow with only its unit, source and scanned input.

Keep a swap run's late leg writes and annotations in its own account

A run started for one account keeps going after an account switch: the
switch unmounts the account's screens, but the run is a closure holding
the manager it started with and never sees the new one. Its group writes
were already kept to its account; its legs, quote tags and transaction
annotations still went through whatever the stores held, so its next leg
was added to the new account's history. Those writes now go to the
account the run started for and are skipped once another is open. The
account-switch test now unmounts the screen's hook, as the app does,
instead of handing it a new manager.

Send a follow list only to the relays its read just covered

A follow list went to every relay in the pool while the read asked only the
write relays, so a pool relay holding a newer list had it replaced. The read
now reports the relays it asked and the publish names exactly those.

Restore only a preview the mint list was opened over

Pay with the mint list dismissed rebuilt a preview from whatever the flow
context held. After an NFC tap had paid a request, opening the mint list and
pressing Pay rebuilt that request's preview and sent it a second time. The
restore now happens only when the list was opened over a preview that still
awaited Pay.

Pin the follow worker against relays that each hold their own lists

The publish fake now lands a list only on the relays it was sent to, or on
every relay in the pool when none is named, as the publish seam does, so a
test can tell a relay that was read from one that was not.

Keep a swap payment pending when its status cannot be read

A melt the mint answered as pending, followed by a status read that threw
(a network error), lost its unsettled mark: the engine returned its
reserved proofs to the wallet and recorded the leg as failed, which the
reconciler then left alone, though the payment could still complete. A
failed read now says nothing about the payment: the engine reads again
until its wait runs out and then leaves the leg payment-pending, its
proofs reserved, for the reconciler. Only the mint reporting the melt
rolled back fails the leg and frees its proofs. A failed read whose
message looked like no route or short inputs no longer leads to a second
route or a second payment either.

Start a mint review afresh, so it cannot carry a paid payment back to Pay

Reviewing an untrusted mint while the machine still sat on a paid melt or a
delivered or undelivered payment request kept that payment's request, amount
and mint. Opening the mint list, choosing a mint or entering an amount from
there rebuilt the old preview, and the next Pay sent it again. A mint review
now starts from a fresh context, except when it interrupts a token receive,
whose scanned input the scan history needs.

Drop a cancelled reroute's late trust answer instead of starting it again

A reroute waiting for its intermediary to be trusted kept going after
Cancel: when the trust arrived it claimed a new run directly, past the
check that another screen's swap holds one, so two runs could move money
at once. A run that was given up now stays given up: the late answer is
dropped, the engine runs nothing and gives the trust back. The check for
whether a run may start is now part of claiming one, so no path claims a
run without it.

Show a swap Pending while any leg can still move, even beside a failed one

The history row returned Failed for any failed leg before asking whether
another leg's melt or mint could still complete, so a swap with money
still moving read as over. The shared outcome now ranks money still
moving first, then a failed leg, then how the run ended, and the detail
screen reads the same value: it shows Failed where the row does, instead
of Complete or Cancelled. The row's earlier pin (a failed leg in a running
group reads Failed) is changed on purpose: that group is Pending.
Format the NFC reader type on one line

Name who holds the NFC reader in one place

The ambient loop, an explicit scan and the payment machine's write-back
each inferred the owner of the tag: the scan source read a module flag
the ambient loop set around each cycle, the session told whichever flow
had last installed a listener, and Tap to pay read the sheet's phase to
decide whether closing it could cancel a payment. A reader hold now
names the holder (ambient or explicit), carries what it wants told when
a tag connects, and is marked writing back when the machine reports it
is creating or writing ecash. All three ask it; the flag, the listener
slot and the listening guards go.

Taking the reader replaces any hold before it and a replaced hold's
release does nothing, so the one difference is a race: a Tap to pay
press started before a blurred wallet's last ambient read has settled
is now explicit (its failures show) where it used to count as ambient.

Pin how the NFC flows share the reader

The scan source keeps an ambient cycle's failed reads quiet and shows
them to an explicit Tap to pay press. The explicit press shows the tap
sheet, turns it to Reading when a tag connects, re-arms while the sheet
stays open, cancels the read when the sheet closes unless the machine
reports that ecash is being created or written, and stops listening
when it ends. A QUIRK pin records that a successful read's own sheet
close cancels the session the write-back then needs.

Keep the redeem failure outcome type private to the orchestrator

Only the orchestrator's own callback type names it; exporting it left
an unused export.

Answer each question about the wallet restore from one decoded status

Nine readers compared the saved restore status by hand, with three
different ideas of which statuses count, and the six values were
spelled out three times. walletRestorePhase now holds the saved values
once, decodes them (undecided, required, an older build's interrupted
run, failed, settled) and answers four questions from one table: safe
to mint (the processors, the redeem drain and its wake-up, nearby
payments), whether recovery is asked (the gate's screen, the prompt
host, a lost database), whether the gate must decide afresh, and
whether a restore is pending (the two prompts). Each reader keeps the
answer it gave; the table shows where they differ. What is saved, and
the store version, are unchanged.

The mirror test of the gate's rules now tests these functions.
Say how an NFC tap ends in the payment machine notes

Release the tag and switch the unit back when an NFC tap throws

A check that threw in the middle of a tap, such as the payment-request
gate failing to read a mint's keysets, went straight to the turn's
safety net: the tag session stayed held and the wallet stayed in the
terminal's unit. The tap now ends first, then the throw goes on to the
safety net as before.

End an NFC tap in one place

The tag session and the unit switch an NFC tap holds were loose locals
of one send() call, released and restored by hand at four of the
auto-resolve loop's exits. They are now one NfcTap value, opened where
the turn starts and ended after the loop: the session is released unless
the write-back already did, and the unit is switched back unless the tap
paid. The two exits that released nothing (no viable option, no mint
candidates) end there too; no tag reaches either today, so nothing a
person sees changes.

Switch back to the wallet's unit when an NFC tap stops for an amount

A tag carrying a USD ecash request beside a sat Lightning invoice
switched the wallet to USD, found no mint able to pay the request, fell
back to the invoice and, in USD, stopped on "must include an amount".
It released the tag but left the wallet in USD. It now switches back,
as every other unpaid end of a tap does.

Pin what every reader of the restore status makes of each saved value

The processors' wait, the redeem drain, the message drain's wake-up,
nearby payments, the two prompts, the prompt host and the restore gate
with no seed, for all six saved statuses. The prompts count unknown,
in-progress and failed as no reason to hold back; the host holds the
queue for failed; the gate keeps a failed status with no seed on the
recovery screen and opens the app for in-progress.

Pin what each end of an NFC tap releases and restores

For a terminal in a unit the host had to switch to: the tag session is
released once at every end, a paid tap keeps the terminal's unit and
every other end switches back. A tap a reset overtook releases and
restores nothing.

Pin the two delivered copies a retry leaves when the first arrives late

A message retried after the 15 second mark and then reported delivered
shows as delivered next to its retried copy; the peer has the text twice
and nothing marks the second as a repeat.

Keep a Bluetooth message delivered when a failure is reported after it

Before: a failure report always won, so a message the peer had
acknowledged could turn back into failed with a retry offer.

After: delivered and read are final, as the owner's ruling that a late
delivery wins implies. Saved data is unchanged.

Show a Bluetooth message delivered when the report comes after 15 seconds

Before: the 15 second watchdog and a relaunch saved an unanswered
message as failed for good, so a delivery reported later was dropped and
the person was offered a retry for a message the peer had; retrying sent
it twice.

After: as the owner ruled, a saved failure whose reason is timeout or
app_restart reads as unconfirmed. It still offers a retry, and a later
sent, delivered or read report wins. A failure the native side reported
stays final. What is saved is unchanged; an older release still reads
these messages as failed.

Move a Bluetooth message's delivery by one table

A message's delivery is sending, sent, delivered, read, unconfirmed
(the watchdog or a restart guessed) or failed (the native side said so),
decoded from the saved status and reason and saved back exactly as
before. Native reports, the 15 second watchdog and a relaunch all move
it through one table in the store, which replaces the status ranks, the
always-accept-failed rule, the watchdog's own read of the store and the
restart's own demotion. Every move is the same as before.

Keep a queued token's saved error as it was on every move but received

Dropping a received token's old error also dropped a saved empty error
on every other move. Only a redeemed entry drops its error now; any
other keeps what it had, as before.

Wait for its retry time before resuming a receive cut short

Before the decode, the drain resumed an interrupted receive only once
the retry time it carried had come; the decode made it resume at once.
An older build keeps that time when it starts the receive, so after a
kill and a clock moved back the entry waited. The redeeming phase now
carries its retry time and the drain waits for it again.

Pin what a Bluetooth message's saved status reads back as

Every saved status and reason is read back as it was saved, except a
sending or sent message, which a relaunch writes as failed with reason
app_restart. A failed message stays failed whatever its reason, also
when the peer reports it delivered after the 15 second watchdog.

Show a queued token's toast for what the queue recorded

The drain called its redeemed and failed callbacks whether or not the
queue took the move, and chose the toast from the error, so a token out
of attempts showed "waiting" while the queue held it as failed.

The queue's moves now say whether they were recorded, and a retry says
whether it ran out. The drain starts a receive only when the queue
recorded the start, reports a receive or a failure only when it was
recorded, and hands the toast what was recorded: waiting while back in
line, failed once held, already redeemed when spent. A refused record
is logged and leaves the toast as it was.

Say where a White Noise conversation stands in one state

The conversation is closed, loading, reading its saved history, ready
with its group or none, creating its group, or failed, and every state
after closed names the client, account and peer it was read for. A send
goes through only when that state is ready or failed for the current
ones, which the loaded-for ref, the group ref and the loading and
creating flags said between them. The screen's fields are read from the
state.

Changed at one edge: when the client is replaced, the old client's group
stops listening at once and a failed read for the new client shows no
group, where before the old group stayed open and usable.

Keep the own-events sync hook compiled

The ??= in 819b670ed made the React Compiler skip the hook; a plain
check and assignment does the same.

Close a held message token as spent only while it is still held

The reconcile reads a held entry, asks the mint, then marks it spent. If
"Receive all" put it back in line meanwhile and the drain started its
receive, the late answer moved the drain's entry to spent under it.
Closing a held entry is now its own move, from held only; an entry back
in line is the drain's, which asks the mint itself.

Leave a token another path queued first to that path

A message carrying a token that also arrived over Bluetooth could pass
its already-known check, wait on the mint-trust lookup, and then park
the Bluetooth entry the drain was receiving: its enqueue was refused as
a duplicate but the park still ran. The receive's own result was then
refused, and the token sat held where no drain, retry or review list
would pick it up.

The message intake now queues a new entry already held or spent, and
writes nothing when the token is queued: only the drain's trust check
moves an entry to untrusted-mint, and no one moves a waiting entry to
spent.

Drop the turn exit that kept the executing flag

Every exit that asked to keep inspect().isExecuting reached it with the
flag already false: each step's work clears it before the turn ends, a
superseded or reset turn never sets it again, and a turn begins with it
cleared. So finishTurn always clears it, and the option goes.

Pin a White Noise send while history is read and after a failed load

While the saved history is read the group is already listening but a
send is refused. After the groups could not be read a send still goes
through, creates a group and points the saved conversation at it.

Finish the turn when a listener throws as Pay starts

A subscriber that threw while the machine announced a melt, a payment
request or an expired quote refresh left the machine held and saying it
was executing, so every later event was dropped. The throw still
reaches the caller and nothing is paid or quoted, as before, but the
turn now finishes and the next Pay runs.

Restore the order a reset, the safety net and Pay finished in

The turn refactor moved three things. A reset again bumps the
generation, reads the unit and goes idle before it frees the machine,
so an event the unit read sends is dropped and a unit read that throws
leaves the machine held, as before. The safety net logs its warning
before it frees the machine and tells listeners. The melt and payment
request tail is inline again, so Pay settles in the microtask after its
last announcement instead of one later; both branches still share one
copy of it.

Pin that own events left unseen mid-switch are written on the next subscription

An event that arrives while the keys and the active account disagree is
not marked seen. When the keys move on first, the account's next
subscription asks the same filters, the relay delivers it again and the
new session writes it.

Keep the saved own profile when a new session sees an equal-time one

Each session started with no memory of the saved profile, so a profile
with the same time and a higher id replaced it at the start of the next
session, though the lower id wins when both arrive together. The
session now starts from the saved profile's time and id.

Never apply an own profile that has no time

Since 8e8608ade a kind 0 whose created_at reads as 0 was applied when it
was the first profile the session saw; before, the session's newest
time started at 0 and such a profile never passed it. It never passes
now either.

End a notification source when an overlapping older page answers newer

Two loadMore calls asking from the same cursor each judged their answer
against the state from before their own request, so a second answer
newer than the first's moved the source back up its history. Each
answer is now judged against where the source stands when it arrives,
as before cec2fb66e.

Pin the follow sync hook and the follow worker together

One test runs the real hook with the real worker over fake relays: a
follow tapped while offline is published once the network is back, and
a later tap publishes a list built on that one.

Follow then unfollow when the button is tapped twice before it redraws

The tap toggled the value the screen last drew, so a second tap before
the redraw recorded a follow again instead of an unfollow. The tap now
toggles what the social store holds at that moment. It moves into a
small hook the screen hands the button, so a test can tap it.

Keep the swap group phase type private to its module

Both screens now read the group through its outcome, so nothing outside
swapGroupPhase.ts names the phase type.

Publish waiting follows when the network comes back

A follow that waited for a relay or an indexer was tried again only on
the next tap, a new list or a return to the foreground, so it could sit
unpublished while the app stayed open. The worker now starts when the
app's offline status turns online, as the ecash redeem queue does, and
does not start while offline. It already started once the NDK and its
signer became ready; a test now pins that.

Keep a follow when signing fails or the signer changes around it

A signer replaced during the read still signed the list, any signing
error dropped the person's taps and showed an error, and a signer
replaced while publishing did not stop the taps being marked done.

The signer is now checked before signing, after signing and after
publishing, and a change at any point keeps the taps for the next pass.
The account's own key is the only signer, so no signing error is a
refusal: a failure keeps the taps like a failed publish does.

Check that a reconciled leg still exists before comparing its operations

The guard from the previous commit read the saved leg's operation ids
after an optional status check, which the type checker rejects: a leg
that is gone and a saved status of none compared equal. A leg that is
gone is now refused first.

Keep a follow when another list lands while it is being published

A list from another client arriving during the publish could be newer
than ours, or from the same second with the id relays prefer, and the
follow was still marked done though the list relays keep did not hold
it. Now, when any list arrived during the publish, the taps stay and
the worker reads again and builds on whatever is newest.

Build a follow again on any list that arrives while it is being signed

The check after signing compared only the list's time, so another
client's list from the same second slipped past and was overwritten.
The worker now checks that the saved list fields are exactly the ones
it built on, which any accepted list or seed changes.

A list dated more than a minute ahead is not built on either, as for
the mute list: ours would be dated there too and relays would keep it
over every later list. The follow waits instead.

Wait for every indexer before treating an account as having no follow list

A first follow on an account with no list published a one-entry list as
soon as the facade's first answer had no list, while Primal or nagg could
still be answering, or had failed, with the person's real list.

The first follow now waits until every enabled source has settled, and
any source that returned a list or failed holds it back. Sources only
say whether they hold a list, never that none exists, so known-empty
still rests on every write relay answering with none and nothing ever
loaded for the account. Sources that all report they serve no list
(nagg's answer for a list it lacks) no longer keep a new account
waiting for ever.

Keep a swap run's late writes out of the next account's history

A run aborted by an account switch ends after the swap history store has
been reset and loaded for the new account, and its cancellation went
through whatever the store held then. Group ids are random, so it found
nothing to change, but nothing tied the write to the account. A swap group
now keeps the account it was started for, its runs carry it, and the
screen's group writes (reopen, finish, cancel) are skipped once the
active account is another. The old account's saved group stays running
and is settled by the reconciler the next time that account is open.

Stop an NFC tap that a reset overtook while it released the tag or the unit

The tap did not check its turn after releasing the tag session or restoring
the person's unit, so a reset during that wait let the old tap carry on: it
ran the handler of the step the reset left and left the machine saying it
was executing. Each of those awaits is now followed by a stale check, and a
stale tap does nothing more. No QUIRK pins remain in the turn exit tests.

Stop decoding the saved follow fields as a list a follow can build on

The saved raw tags share their stamp with nagg and Primal seeds, so a
seed with the same people could make old tags and content read as the
newest list. Follows now build only on what a complete relay read just
returned, so the decode only says whether a list or seed was ever loaded
for the account and how new the newest one was. What is saved does not
change.

Record an NFC tap's payment before linking it, so Pay cannot send it again

After an NFC tap paid a request, a link that threw left the step on the
unpaid payment request preview, and a later Pay sent the request a second
time. The tap now records the settlement first and links through the same
logging helper as Pay, so it completes on the sent screen whatever the link
does.

Finish the turn and keep a payment paid when what follows it throws

If linking the transaction, a notification or a listener threw between a
melt or payment request result and its handler, Pay rejected and the machine
stayed held and "executing" until a reset, and a delivered request's caller
saw only the error. The step now records the outcome first; links and
notifications run through one helper that logs a throw instead of passing it
on, and the turn always finishes. A throwing listener still reaches the
caller, after the outcome is recorded and the machine is free.

Never build a follow list on a read that did not reach every write relay

A follow or unfollow could overwrite people already on the public list:
the worker kept whatever list arrived before a timeout, and then built on
the saved list whatever the read had returned. An older relay answering
while the relay with the newer list timed out made the next follow drop
everyone added since.

Publishing and settling a tap the list already holds now stand only on
the list a complete read of every write relay just returned. A partial
read is never saved and the taps wait. When the account is known to have
a newer list or seed than any write relay holds, or had one that no write
relay has any more, the taps wait too.

Apply a reconciled swap result only to the attempt it was read for

Before, the reconciler checked only that a leg's status had not changed
while it read the leg's melt or mint. A retry for short inputs prepares a
new melt while the leg stays at invoiceReady, and a retried leg can come
back to settling with a new mint, so a rolled-back first melt could fail
the leg whose second melt was being paid, and an old mint could mark a
new attempt done. It now writes only while the status and both operation
ids are the ones it read. A reconciler that was stopped (a new manager)
also writes nothing, even from a pass that was mid-read.

Refuse a second swap by who owns a run, and show the toast for a retry

Before, a retry after the ended toast had been dismissed ran with no
toast at all, and the "another swap is running" refusal looked only at
the toast: a swiped-away toast let a second swap start beside a running
one, a retry never checked, and a toast left running with no run behind
it blocked every start. Now start, retry, retry-failed and route-through
are refused while any screen's run owns a swap group, and a retry shows
the group's toast again when there is none, with each leg as the screen
has it.

Keep a newer payment's lock when Pay with no mint chosen finishes late

Pay tapped on the mint list with no mint chosen re-runs the list's handler,
then freed the machine without asking whether its turn still held it. When a
newer turn had taken over meanwhile, its lock was released under it, so a
second Pay could run while the newer turn waited for its quote. That exit now
checks ownership like every other, which retires finishTurn's unguarded
option. A confirm caller's result is also taken by its own turn as it begins,
so a tap that sent nothing is told `ignored`, not a later tap's "delivered".

Keep Pay offered when a payment request entry only carries its preview id

The screen entry merge marked a payment request preview delivered as soon as
any operation id appeared, its own preview id included, which hid Pay on a
request that never sent. The merge now asks the one phase decoder, which
does not count a preview id as an operation. Melt entries, which share the
merge, are promoted exactly as before.

Keep a paid or sent payment preview from turning back into one Pay sends again

Once a melt was paid, or a payment request delivered or sent and not taken
back, choosing a mint, entering an amount or choosing the option again rebuilt
an unpaid preview, and the next Pay sent the money a second time. A settled
preview is now final for its flow: only an event that starts another flow
leaves it, and every other event changes nothing. One exhaustive table
replaces the three separate guards for Pay and the mint list.

Settle a swap leg left holding a prepared melt from that melt

Before, a leg saved at invoiceReady with a melt (the app died after the
melt was prepared, or during a retry for short inputs, which pays from
invoiceReady) was never read again, and its group could never close
because a melt existed. Now the reconciler treats it like a melting leg
once no run owns its group: a finalized melt moves it to settling and on,
a rolled-back melt fails it, and anything unresolved or unreadable leaves
it. The leg table gains the one move that needs, invoiceReady to settling.
No saved value changes.

Keep a swap Pending while any of its payments can still complete

Before, a swap whose run was aborted or cancelled while a leg was still
melting or verifying read Completed in the list and Cancelled, with
everything sent counted as fees, on its detail screen, though its melt
could still be paid. Now one function decides what both show: a leg
melting, verifying, settling, payment pending, or holding an invoice with
a melt keeps the swap Pending (Running on the detail screen) however the
group was saved. The reconciler closes an interrupted group by the same
rule. A failed leg still reads Failed first, as before.

Drop an earlier attempt's error when a queued token is received

A token received after a failed attempt kept that attempt's error, in
memory and in what the queue saved. It is now left out once the entry is
redeemed; the field stays in the schema, and a spent or refused entry
still records its error.

Refuse a redeem queue move that has no meaning

The store took any status from any status, so a late answer could undo a
settled entry: a spent probe still out when this wallet received the
token turned it from redeemed to spent, a message intake racing the
Bluetooth one could park a received token for review, and "try again"
landing on a token being received reset it to never tried.

One table in wallet/redeemEntry names the statuses each move may start
from (every move the intakes, the drain, try again, receive all and the
reconcile make), and markStatus, scheduleRetry and requeue refuse and log
any other. Test setup that made a refused entry straight from pending now
goes through the drain's start, as the app does.

Give each payment machine turn one way in and one way out

send() now begins with beginTurn and leaves through finishTurn, which
frees the machine only while the turn still owns it. The lock, the
executing flag, the commit generation and the payment request confirm
holders are written only by the small set of turn functions, so no exit
releases them by hand any more. The melt and payment request branches
share one tail. Behaviour is unchanged; the quirks pinned in
turn-exits.test.ts are marked where they live.

Read a redeem queue entry through one decoded phase

The entry's status union was spelled out in the store, the orchestrator
and the strike state, and six status strings were compared across the
readers. wallet/redeemEntry (a dependency-free subpath, like
wallet/units) now holds the statuses, the attempt limit, the entry type
and meshRedeemPhase: waiting (with its retry time), redeeming, redeemed,
spent, untrusted-mint, failed (refused or out of retries). The store's
schema, the drain, the strike map, the message ecash lists and the drain
log read through it. What is saved is unchanged.

Pin the turn exits a superseded handler, quote refresh or early throw reach

An older turn's handler or quote refresh that returns late must not free
the newer turn's lock, and a throw before the handler runs is swallowed
with the machine free. Pinned as a quirk: when linking a paid NFC tap
throws, the step stays on the payment request preview and a later Pay
sends the request again. Each pin was seen to pass on the code before
the turn refactor and to fail when that exit is broken.

Choose the same own profile however its events arrive in batches

Before: a profile event with the same time as the one already applied
and a lower id was ignored when it came in a later batch, though it won
when both came together, so the cached name and picture depended on
batching.

After: the sync keeps the newest profile's time and id and admits a
later one by the same order the batch and the Nostr package use
(newer, then lower id).

Pin what each exit of a payment machine turn leaves behind

Whether the next event runs, what a waiting payment request confirm
resolves with, and whether the machine still says it is executing, for
every way out of send(). Five quirks pinned as they are: a superseded
Pay with no mint frees the newer turn's lock and shares its confirm
result, a throw while linking a paid melt or delivered request keeps the
machine held, and an NFC tap reset while releasing its session carries
on and leaves the machine saying it executes.

Pin every redeem queue move, what each reader makes of an entry, and the interrupted drop

Each writer's move through the store (intakes, drain, try again, receive
all, reconcile), what the message ecash readers say for every kind of
entry, which entries a drain picks, and F213 as it is today: a drop the
app was killed in the middle of ends spent with a red toast and no sender.

Never write one account's own events into another account's stores

Before: after an in-process account switch, own events the subscription
still held for the previous account were written into the new account's
likes, reposts, replies, notes and deletions, and while the keys lagged
the switch every new own event went into the stores of the account just
switched to.

After: the sync dispatches only events signed by its session's account,
and only while that account is the active one. Until the keys and the
active account agree it writes nothing and keeps the batch, which is
dispatched once they do. The profile and follow list checks this makes
redundant go.

Keep the own-events sync's memory in one session per account

What the sync has dispatched and the newest profile time it applied now
live in one session that belongs to an account, made when that
account's keys appear and replaced when they change, instead of two refs
cleared by one effect and read by another. What is written is unchanged.

Pin what the own-events sync writes while the keys lag an account switch

With the active account already changed and the keys still the previous
account's, a like is written into the loaded stores and the profile and
follow list are refused. Pinned as a quirk.

Name where each notification source stands in paging

Each source is now pending, ready or in backoff with the cursor to ask
from, exhausted, unsupported, or failed on its first page, in the feed
pager's words, and one step function moves it on each answer. The
exhausted flag, the missing-entry meaning pending and the cursor guard
the type now proves go. Paging asks the same sources as before; the
source log line names the state it moved to.

Pin which notification sources are asked for older pages

A source whose first page failed, one that cannot serve notifications,
and one still on its first page when the list painted are each pinned:
the first two are never asked again in the session, the last joins
paging once it answers. The failed first page is pinned as a quirk.
Keep the saved swap group's state type private to its store

Move a saved swap leg only along the order a transfer takes

A leg's saved status now follows a table: an invoice, then the melt,
then the destination's mint, with failed reachable from any step. Done
is final, a failed leg goes again only through a new invoice, and a leg
whose money has left never returns to before its melt. Moves the table
does not list are refused and logged. An error message can only be
saved with a failure. No writer in the app makes a refused move today;
the store's own pin that took a failed leg straight to done now goes
through a new attempt.

Never let a follow replace the follow list with one the app cannot vouch for

Tapping Follow published a list built from the saved raw tags, which
were empty or older whenever the shown follows came from nagg or Primal,
so the person's whole public follow list was replaced by one entry. A
follow interrupted by closing the app stayed pending and the button
ignored every later tap.

A tap now only records the intent and the button shows it at once. One
worker per account reads the newest signed list from every write relay,
applies only the outstanding intents to its tags and content exactly as
read, and publishes. With nothing it can stand on (only a seed, or a
read that did not finish and no saved list) it publishes nothing and the
follow waits; a brand-new account counts as empty only when every write
relay and the indexers say there is no list. Intents saved before a
restart are resumed once the account loads, and again on each tap, when
a list arrives and on returning to the foreground. A failed publish keeps
the intent; a signer that refuses drops it and shows the error. The
account and signer are checked after every wait.

The single-flight guard, the in-flight flag and the busy state on the
button go: every tap counts.

Name the own follow list's states where the social store is read

The saved contact fields decode into unknown, seeded (pubkeys from nagg
or Primal that the saved raw list does not match) or authoritative (the
raw list the follow set was read from), and a pending follow entry
decodes as an outstanding intent, also after a restart. What is saved
does not change. setFollowIntent and settleFollowIntents are what the
follow worker will use; nothing reads the new shapes yet.

Settle a swap interrupted by an app kill from its own operations

Before, a swap whose run was gone (the app killed mid-run) stayed Pending
for good: the reconciler skipped its legs at melting or verifying because
the group was saved as running, and never ended the group. Now a group
saved as running that no run in this process holds has its legs settled
from their melt and mint operations like an ended run's, and once every
leg is at rest it is ended: finished when each leg reached an outcome,
cancelled when one stopped before sending anything. A leg whose melt may
still complete keeps the group running.

End a swap's group, toast and screen together, however its run ends

Before, a rebalance that threw or was aborted by an account switch left
its saved group running for good (and the toast spinning, which blocked
the next swap), and a retry that succeeded after Cancel left the group
and toast cancelled. Now the screen owns one run at a time and holds its
group while it does: the run's end, a throw, an abort or Cancel gives it
up and ends the group, the screen and its own toast as one. A retry
reopens the group and its toast and ends them again. A saved group ends
once: finished and cancelled never replace each other; no new value is
written.
Say plainly why an operation id outranks the entry's phase

Keep the payment request entry phase type inside its module

Nothing outside reads the type by name, and knip flags it as an unused
export.

End a progress toast once, and drop a leg's error when it succeeds

Before, a leg that failed and then succeeded on a retry kept the old
error, and a toast that had ended could be turned into another ending
(cancelled then done). Legs and the run now move only along a table:
done and skipped legs are final, an error lives only on a failed leg,
and an ended run is reopened only by resume, which a retry calls.

Read a saved swap group as running, interrupted, finished or cancelled

A group saved as running is only running while a run in this process
holds it; otherwise it is interrupted. The phase is decided where the
group is read, so nothing new is saved. The row, the detail screen and
the reconciler switch on it; what they show and do is unchanged.

Do not count a payment request as delivered by its preview id

Before: any operation id on the payment request entry counted as
delivered. A rolled-back send, which carries the preview id as its
operation id, offered no Cancel, and a preview carrying its own id
offered neither Pay nor Cancel.
After: the preview's own id names no operation, and a rolled-back entry
offers Cancel (still no Pay). Delivered and undelivered entries keep
offering neither.

Pin how a swap run ends, how its saved legs reconcile and what its row says

Records as quirks what F211 describes: a run that throws or is aborted
leaves its group running, a leg such a run left at melting or verifying
is never reconciled, a retry after Cancel leaves the group cancelled and
the toast untouched, and a progress leg keeps an old error.

Read the payment request entry's phase in one place

The payment request screen entry's phase strings are now decoded by one
function into preview, delivered, undelivered, rolled back or
unrecognised, and written for a send's outcome by one function beside
it. Availability and the payment request screen switch on the decoded
phase; the two copies of the preview test and the three hand-built
entries in the confirm handler are gone. The strings written are
unchanged, so the timeline reads what it read before.

Share the mute list's safe read of an own replaceable list

The read that waits for every write relay, the event check and the
account and signer guards move out of the mute-list code unchanged, so
the follow list can be read and replaced the same way. The read now
reports how it ended (complete, timed out, failed, no relays) with the
newest event seen; the mute list still refuses anything but complete.

Receive a follow list or profile last changed more than a year ago

The own-events subscription asked for every kind with a one-year since,
which relays apply to the profile and follow list too, so an older list
never arrived and the follow button had nothing to build on. Kinds 0
and 3 now have their own unwindowed newest-only filters; the history
kinds keep the window and the cap.

A follow list written by another account is no longer saved as this
account's, also when it is newer than the own one in the same batch.

Give the payment preview steps a required phase

The melt and payment request preview steps now say whether they await
Pay, settled (with the history entry) or, for a payment request, left
undelivered (with the operation id), in one required tagged phase.
The optional historyEntry and undeliveredOperationId fields are gone;
the confirm and mint list guards switch on the phase, and every place
that builds these steps writes it.

Pin what tapping Follow publishes today

The screen's follow toggle against the real social store: the saved list
is kept with the new entry, an unfollow removes one entry, and the
quirks the follow repair will change (a seeded or empty list publishes
one entry, a failed publish snaps back, a pending entry saved before a
kill locks the button, other entries are deduplicated).

Pin what the payment request entry says after each send outcome

Pins the whole entry the confirm handler writes when a send is delivered,
not taken back, or rolled back; Pay and Cancel for every phase the entry
can carry; and a confirm after the mint list was opened and closed on an
unpaid payment request preview.

Match the selector test to the White Noise setup button's new wiring

630d49acf made the setup button await bootstrap, whose result the banner
now reads. The source check still looked for the old bare handler.

Do not send a payment request again after ecash left and was not taken back

Before: after a send whose ecash was created, not confirmed delivered and
not reclaimed, the machine still ran the send again on the next confirm.
The default screen hid Pay, but the machine itself did not refuse.
After: the step records the operation and ignores a further confirm or a
mint list request. Found in review of e78e21e3c.

Keep a failed White Noise setup on screen when its key package was stored

Before: a key package that was stored but refused by the relays raised the
local count to the target, and the card with the error disappeared.
After: a failure stays up with its error. Found in review of 630d49acf.

Refuse a White Noise send in the moment the client first arrives

Before: a screen opened before the White Noise client existed could send
in the commit that first carried the client, before the saved conversation
was read, creating a second group and overwriting the saved one.
After: a send goes through only once a read has finished for this client
and this person. Found in review of 8f25cd414.

Do not apply a theme that was cancelled while its wallpaper downloaded

Before: tapping Cancel while Apply was still downloading the main wallpaper
closed the editor, but when the download finished the cancelled theme was
saved anyway, any theme draft opened since was wiped, and the screen went
back a second time.

After: an Apply whose draft was cancelled (or replaced by a new one) during
the download saves nothing, leaves the newer draft as it is and does not
navigate. An Apply that is not cancelled saves exactly as before.

Stop watching an acceleration after its screen closed or its transaction changed

Before: if the acceleration invoice came back after the send screen closed or
the transaction id changed, the old request still started a status poll,
could stop the new transaction's poll, and a late acknowledgement could
still mark the melt accelerated.

After: invoice and status results belong to the screen and transaction that
asked for them; once that owner is gone they start no poll, leave the
current poll alone and save nothing. The invoice is still handed back to the
caller as before.

Keep a mint's newest keyset units when an older read finishes late

Before: if coco refreshed a mint while the first read of its keyset units
was still running, the older read could finish last and overwrite the newer
answer, so a unit the mint now supports could disappear (or one it dropped
could come back) until the next refresh.

After: only the newest read for the mounted wallet publishes; an older read
that finishes afterwards is ignored.

Stop showing a closed DM feed's load error

Before: when a DM feed failed to load and then could no longer be loaded at
all (signed out of Nostr, or no counterparty), its rows and spinners were
cleared but the old load error was still reported beside the idle state.

After: the error is cleared with the rest of that feed's state, so an idle
feed reports no error.

Try again to replace a paid onchain address when the first try fails

Before: when a payment reached the standing onchain address and the mint
refused the replacement address, the receive tab recorded the address as
already replaced and never asked again while it stayed open, so the paid
address kept being shown for the next payer.

After: rotate reports whether the replacement was recorded; a failed one
releases the address, and the next mempool report of the same paid address
asks the mint again. A report while a rotation is still running still does
not start a second one.

Offer no other way to pay when ecash left and could not be taken back

Before: a payment request whose ecash was created, not confirmed delivered
and not reclaimed still moved a multi-option payment to its other options,
where paying could pay the recipient twice.
After: the failure is reported and the flow stays where it is. Found in
review of 126bd625f.

Do not open the mint list from a payment that has already settled

Before: opening and closing the mint list after a paid melt or a delivered
payment request rebuilt the preview without its settled entry, so a second
Pay ran the payment again.
After: a settled preview ignores the mint list request. Found in review of
e62206d6f.

Keep a delivered payment request delivered when its history row cannot be read

Before: a send that reached the recipient, followed by a failed history
read, was reported as failed and Pay was offered again.
After: the fallback entry stands in for the row and the send is reported
as delivered. Found in review of 126bd625f.

Keep loading older notifications after one page fails to load

Before: when a page of older notifications failed (a timeout or a network
error), that source was treated as having no more history, so scrolling to
the bottom never asked it again for the rest of the visit.

After: a failed page keeps the source's place, and the next scroll to the
bottom asks for the same page again, as the home feed already does. Paging
ends only when a source reports the end of its history or cannot page.

Show why White Noise setup failed instead of a success check

Before: when publishing the key packages failed, the setup card on Contacts
still played its green check and faded out, then came back later with no
word of what went wrong.

After: the check plays only when setup finished. A failed setup keeps the
card, shows the error under its description, and "Set up" tries again.

Keep the White Noise send box closed until the conversation has loaded

Before: a message sent while a White Noise chat was still loading did not
know a group already existed, so it created a second group, invited the peer
again (spending one of their key packages and putting a second request in
their inbox) and pointed the saved conversation at the new group.

After: the send box stays disabled while the conversation loads, and a send

Show a background send or melt confirmation in the payment's own unit

sheet's error text and then closed the sheet in the same finally block, so
nothing was imported and nothing was shown.

popup; an invalid key stays in the sheet beside the error.

Run every startup recovery even when an earlier one fails

Routstr recoveries that run after the wallet opens. If send recovery threw,
none of the others ran for that launch, including the Routstr refund recovery
that has a deadline.

Give each recovery its own failure handling: a failure is logged with its
phase and reported as before, and the next recovery still runs. The order is
unchanged. The comment that said the Routstr refund recovery runs first now
describes where it actually runs.

Keep a rotation visible to later ensures after the quote flights are disposed

The per-manager flight map is replaced on dispose. A rotation that was waiting
for an ensure when that happened registered itself in the old map, so the next
ensure for the same wallet could not see it and created a third quote.

Look the map up after the wait.

Redact secrets in an Error nested inside logged params

Only an Error passed as a top-level log param had its message and stack run
through the known-secret redaction. One nested in an object, array, Map or Set
was written out as is, so a key or token quoted in the message reached the
ring buffer and the log file.

Apply the same redaction where nested errors are compacted.

Give each wallet its own reusable quote when two ask at once

The single-flight map for standing quotes was keyed by mint, method and unit
only. A second wallet manager that asked while the first one's create was
still running got the first manager's promise: its quote and address, with
nothing created or recorded for the second wallet.

Keep the in-flight map per manager, as the resolved cache beside it already
is, and only clear a slot that still holds the task that is finishing.

Return a receive's own history row when another row was saved first

The receive and mint-quote factories looked for the saved history row with one
find() whose predicate accepted either this operation's row or any row that
was new since the snapshot. A different receive or quote from the same mint
that sat earlier in the page was returned instead, so the caller got another
operation's id, and for a mint quote another quote's payment request.

Look for the exact operation or quote across the whole page first, and only
then fall back to a row that is new since the snapshot.
